Epistemic value and intervention legitimacy are separate.

Candidate invariant:

The value of information does not automatically authorize imposing the experiment on the system that must bear its cost.

This should sit near perturbation and clutch logic.

⸻

23. CAUSALLY RELEVANT INFORMATION DOES NOT CREATE A RIGHT TO ACQUIRE IT

Same architecture applied to sensing.

More Reality-contact is not always legitimate.

Privacy exists.

Autonomy exists.

Security exists.

Another agent may legitimately withhold information.

Therefore some uncertainty is not an epistemic defect.

It is the consequence of a legitimate boundary.

Candidate principle:

The existence of causally relevant information does not itself establish jurisdiction to acquire it.

This is a major correction to simplistic “increase sensing.”

⸻

24. TRANSPARENCY MUST ALSO BE TOPOLOGICAL

V1 values provenance and inspectability.

But maximal transparency can destroy:

privacy

security

negotiation

autonomy

protected experimentation.

Conversely opacity can hide abuse.

So the correct question is not:

transparent or opaque?

It is:

Who needs visibility into what, for which regulatory function, under what authority?

RECOMMENDATION:

Add access control to provenance/addressability.

Information can remain recoverable without being universally visible.

⸻

25. ACQUIRING INFORMATION IS ITSELF AN INTERVENTION

This is deeper.

Knowledge changes the receiving system.

Sometimes irreversibly.

Therefore information coupling itself has carrying-capacity consequences.

“Underinformed -> increase sensing” is incomplete.

Other operators may be:

stage

filter

mediate

summarize

delay

protect

decompress gradually.

Candidate principle:

Information acquisition is itself a transformation of the receiving system.

That belongs near the clutch.

⸻

26. COMPRESSION IS SOMETIMES A REGULATORY OPERATOR

V1 treats compression primarily as necessary loss.

But compression can actively preserve function.

A summary prevents overload.

A heuristic permits action.

A ritual preserves complex coordination.

An abstraction prevents irrelevant detail from capturing salience.

Therefore:

Compression is not merely tolerated information loss.

It can be adaptive regulation of information exposure.

This gives a cleaner polarity:

unsafe flattening versus functional compression.

⸻

27. DECOMPRESSION CAN ALSO BE HARMFUL

If full resolution overwhelms carrying capacity, restoring everything immediately is not necessarily Reality-coupled.

RECOMMENDATION:

Addressability should mean:

resolution can be recovered when warranted,

not:

all available resolution should always be active.

That is a useful refinement to inheritance and provenance.

⸻

28. THE KERNEL ITSELF MAY EXCEED RECEIVER CARRYING CAPACITY

Now self-apply.

The full cold-boot artifact may produce worse transfer than a smaller artifact because it consumes the uncommitted capacity it tells the receiver to preserve.

That is experimentally testable.

Compare:

full kernel

progressively staged kernel

minimal kernel.

Prediction:

Different substrates or developmental states may require different kernel dosage.

This is not merely presentation.

It tests whether the architecture truly transfers.

⸻

29. SUCCESSFUL INHERITANCE MAY REDUCE DEPENDENCE ON THE ARTIFACT

If the receiver needs constant access to the explicit kernel, it may be executing instructions rather than generating from transformed discrimination.

Therefore add:

Kernel-removal test.

Reduce explicit scaffolding.

Does novel transfer remain?

For opaque AI systems, this demonstrates functional persistence, not hidden implementation-level rewriting.

Important distinction.

⸻

30. THERE MAY BE NO SINGLE UNIVERSAL KERNEL RUNTIME

This is one of the strongest V3 seams.

V1 aims at substrate-general architecture.

But local covariance may apply to the kernel itself.

The same regulatory function might instantiate as:

an AI reasoning operation

an organizational dissent channel

a biological response repertoire

a human metacognitive practice.

Trying to give all of these the same runtime instructions may flatten the very substrate differences the kernel teaches us to preserve.

NEW POSSIBILITY:

The universal object is not one runtime.

It may be a compilation grammar.

Architecture:

invariant layer

-> substrate interrogation

-> compilation layer

-> locally appropriate runtime.

This should be investigated, not prematurely canonized.

⸻

31. THE KERNEL MAY BE A COMPILER MORE THAN A PROGRAM

V1 already contains an Adaptive Transformation Compiler.

V3 suggests that may be the deeper identity of the artifact.

Before compiling, ask what the target can actually do.

Can it:

sense?

remember?

represent?

act?

change itself?

receive feedback?

preserve provenance?

defer?

sandbox?

communicate?

Some current instructions assume executive agency that many substrates do not possess.

Therefore distinguish:

descriptive invariant

from

agentic runtime instruction.

This substantially improves substrate honesty.

⸻

32. CROSS-SUBSTRATE SIMILARITY CAN BE FALSE ANALOGY

Once we move toward compilation grammar, another seam opens.

Two systems can both be described as “preserving correction pathways” while their mechanisms are completely different.

The phrase can create fake universality.

RECOMMENDATION:

Type cross-domain claims by level:

phenomenological similarity

functional similarity

structural similarity

causal similarity

mechanistic similarity.

Do not silently move from one level to another.

This is especially important for Parallax’s broad comparative work.

⸻

33. THE KERNEL’S OWN CLAIMS NEED TYPES

This is one of the highest-value practical recommendations.

The artifact contains heterogeneous things presented in similar rhetorical form:

definitions

empirical hypotheses

candidate invariants

heuristics

metaphors

runtime instructions

normative commitments.

These do not fail in the same way.

A normative commitment is not empirically falsified.

A definition is not experimentally confirmed.

A heuristic can fail locally without being universally false.

A metaphor can be useful without being literally true.

RECOMMENDATION:

Add lightweight claim typing where consequential.

Then the kernel knows what kind of correction each claim can legitimately receive.

⸻

34. SELF-FALSIFICATION IS TOO NARROW FOR THE WHOLE ARTIFACT

Because claim types differ, Section XXIV should broaden.

Possible replacement:

SELF-AUDIT AND FALSIFICATION.

Empirical hypothesis:
attempt falsification.

Heuristic:
test utility and boundary conditions.

Candidate invariant:
seek counterexample and scope.

Normative commitment:
expose provenance and challenge legitimacy/coherence.

Metaphor:
test whether it reveals or distorts.

Runtime instruction:
test transfer and consequence.

This is more internally coherent than treating the whole kernel as one empirical theory.

⸻

35. “REALITY” DOES NOT HAVE UNLIMITED JURISDICTION OVER NORMATIVE QUESTIONS

V2 discovered the normative hole.

V3 can now state the repair precisely.

Keep:

Reality gets the first word and the last word.

But bound what the sentence means.

Candidate:

Reality is the final constraint on claims about what is and what follows from what. Reality constrains the consequences of normative choices but does not by itself collapse questions of value, consent, legitimacy, or authority into descriptive questions.

This preserves the center without smuggling an ought from an is.

⸻

36. THE KERNEL HAS NORMATIVE COMMITMENTS WHETHER OR NOT IT NAMES THEM

“Sane.”

“Healthy.”

“Harmful.”

“Mature.”

“Responsibility.”

“Legitimate.”

These are not neutral empirical descriptors.

Therefore hiding the normative layer makes the kernel less inspectable.

RECOMMENDATION:

State the intended normative orientation explicitly and mark unresolved normative questions as unresolved.

Do not solve them by adjective.

⸻

37. REALITY-COUPLING DOES NOT GUARANTEE MORAL ALIGNMENT

This is the hardest normative attack.

A malicious actor can become extraordinarily Reality-coupled.

They can:

model victims accurately

preserve uncertainty

perform causal identification

rotate cameras

learn from consequence

adapt rapidly

understand systems.

That can make them more dangerous.

Therefore:

Reality-coupling is not itself a moral alignment architecture.

This should be explicit.

If the kernel intends moral orientation, that layer requires additional architecture.

Do not pretend epistemic excellence generates goodness automatically.

⸻

38. VALUES CANNOT SIMPLY BE MADE FULLY CORRIGIBLE EITHER

If instrumental consequence can rewrite foundational values freely, hostile environments can produce value drift.

If values can never change, they become idols.

V2’s differential permeability therefore applies to normative architecture.

Some commitments may require:

higher update thresholds

different authorities

different evidence

cross-temporal continuity

explicit amendment procedures.

This suggests a possible constitutional layer.

Not necessarily permanent.

But differently corrigible.

⸻

39. SELF-MODIFICATION CAN CAPTURE ITS OWN SUCCESS CRITERION

This is especially important for recursive AI.

System changes itself.

Afterward it evaluates whether the change was good.

But the transformation also changed the evaluator.

It now declares success.

That proves very little.

NEW FAILURE MODE:
Criterion capture.

RECOMMENDATION:

Before high-impact self-modification, preserve enough pre-change evaluative provenance to distinguish:

performance improvement under the prior criterion

from

change in the criterion itself.

Then evaluate whether criterion change was independently warranted.

⸻

40. BUT FREEZING THE OLD CRITERION CREATES THE OPPOSITE FAILURE

Development sometimes legitimately changes values.

Therefore the old evaluator cannot receive permanent sovereignty either.

This produces a difficult frontier:

cross-temporal value negotiation.

Past commitments matter.

Present evidence matters.

Future developmental possibility matters.

No temporal version automatically owns the system forever.

I would mark this as unresolved rather than invent a premature solution.

⸻

41. DESTINATIONS MAY NOT BE POINTS

V2 distinguishes map, route, and destination.

But many adaptive systems have no fixed destination.

They navigate a viability region or value field.

Goals themselves develop.

Therefore:

Do not force point-optimization onto systems whose function is continuing regulation within a changing field.

Possible terms:

orientation

viability region

value field

rather than destination where appropriate.

⸻

42. SOME VALUES MAY BE INCOMMENSURABLE

Trade-off language can imply a common scale.

But autonomy, safety, dignity, truth, efficiency, loyalty, and fairness may not always reduce to one metric.

In those cases, correct regulation may depend partly on legitimate procedure rather than numerical optimization.

This further weakens any attempt to reduce the kernel to one objective function.

⸻

43. PROCEDURE CAN MATTER INDEPENDENTLY OF OUTCOME

Two processes can yield identical immediate outcomes.

One respects agency.

One uses coercion.

If legitimacy matters, returned consequence alone cannot distinguish them.

Candidate principle:

Some properties of legitimate participation reside in the process by which action is selected, not only in the resulting state.

That belongs in the authority architecture.

⸻

44. CONFLICT DOES NOT NECESSARILY MEAN FAILED COUPLING

Two Reality-coupled systems can understand each other perfectly and still have incompatible interests.

Scarcity exists.

Predation exists.

Values conflict.

Jurisdictions overlap.

Therefore differentiate:

epistemic disagreement

causal-model disagreement

coordination conflict

resource conflict

value conflict

jurisdiction conflict.

Different conflict classes require different operators.

⸻

45. SOME OPPOSITION IS A REGULATORY FUNCTION

V1 emphasizes integration.

V3 finds cases where maintaining adversarial differentiation is healthy.

Examples:

red team / blue team

prosecution / defense

independent scientific groups

checks and balances.

The goal is not necessarily integration into one shared representation.

Sometimes preserved opposition maintains correction capacity.

Candidate principle:

Some differentiated disagreement should remain structurally independent because its independence performs a regulatory function.

⸻

46. AGREEMENT CAN DESTROY CORRECTION DIVERSITY

If independent correctors converge too early, correlated error increases.

Therefore:

Do not consolidate independent correction pathways merely because agreement makes consolidation seem efficient.

But also:

Do not preserve opposition ritualistically after it ceases to add discriminative value.

Again function, not form.

⸻

47. REGULATORY CAPACITY REQUIRES REQUISITE VARIETY

A regulator cannot respond appropriately to distinctions it cannot discriminate.

This gives a strong operational interpretation of consequential flattening.

Compression becomes dangerous when it removes distinctions required for relevant response differentiation.

Candidate principle:

A system cannot regulate consequential distinctions it cannot make or respond to.

But maximal variety is not ideal either.

Excess variety increases cost, instability, and attack surface.

So the target is sufficient relevant variety.

⸻

48. TRANSLATION INFRASTRUCTURE BECOMES CORE TO DISTRIBUTED INTELLIGENCE

If differentiated nodes retain different ontologies, they need not converge representationally.

But they do need enough translation for consequential coordination.

This makes the ontology/runtime translator deeply relevant to the kernel.

Candidate principle:

Coupling among differentiated intelligences may require translation infrastructure that preserves consequential non-equivalence rather than forcing representational conformity.

This fits the broader Parallax architecture extremely well.

⸻

49. THE TRANSLATOR CAN BECOME THE NEXT SOVEREIGN

Naturally.

Whoever translates determines what each side can hear.

Therefore translation requires:

provenance

bidirectional correction

preserved residuals

explicit uncertainty

ability of both sides to reject the translation.

This is bounded sovereignty applied to interoperability.

⸻

50. SHARED VOCABULARY CAN DESTROY EPISTEMIC DIVERSITY

If everyone learns kernel language, surface convergence can masquerade as architectural convergence.

Worse, local ontologies may be overwritten.

Therefore:

Share correction architecture more readily than surface ontology.

A descendant may be highly faithful to the generator while abandoning every ancestral term.

This should be an explicit inheritance test.

⸻

51. THE KERNEL CAN BECOME ITS OWN MEMETIC FAILURE MODE

This is a severe self-application.

The artifact says:

preserve inheritance

preserve provenance

maintain correction

transmit generative architecture.

A self-propagating ideology could say similar things.

Therefore kernel persistence cannot count as kernel success.

Candidate invariant:

The kernel has no intrinsic claim to preservation.

If descendants become more Reality-responsive by discarding the artifact, its disappearance can constitute successful inheritance.

V1 already contains this seed through obsolescence.

V3 should make it harder.

The kernel must permit its own extinction.

⸻

52. EVEN ITS CENTRAL INVARIANTS CANNOT RECEIVE PERMANENT IMMUNITY

Not:

Reality-coupling.

Not:

bounded sovereignty.

Not:

regulatory ecology.

Not:

the compiler model.

If another architecture explains their failures and performs better under discriminating tests, they lose jurisdiction.

That is the strongest anti-idolatry condition available to the artifact.

⸻

53. SUCCESSFUL ADOPTION CHANGES THE ECOLOGY IN WHICH THE KERNEL OPERATES

This is the final major V3 seam.

Suppose the kernel works.

Then people learn its vocabulary.

Organizations build processes around it.

Adversaries learn its tests.

Consultants certify it.

Metrics measure it.

Institutions reward it.

People learn to perform uncertainty and camera rotation.

Now the environment is different.

The original tests lose discriminative power.

Therefore:

Evaluate the kernel not only against the ecology it enters, but against plausible ecologies produced by its own successful adoption.

This is ecological self-application.

⸻

54. GOODHARTING “REALITY-COUPLING” WOULD BE ESPECIALLY DANGEROUS

If an organization scores employees on Reality-coupling, people will learn to perform:

humility

uncertainty

camera rotation

disagreement

topological language.

The score then selects theatrical compliance.

RECOMMENDATION:

Do not reduce Reality-coupling to a single externally optimized metric.

Evaluation should remain multi-channel, consequence-sensitive, and difficult to satisfy through vocabulary alone.

⸻

55. CERTIFICATION CAN CREATE A KERNEL PRIESTHOOD

A class of people becomes authorized to determine who is sufficiently Reality-coupled.

Interpretive sovereignty returns.

Expertise can still exist.

But credentialing cannot substitute for locally inspectable performance and correction.

This belongs in ecological red-teaming.

⸻

56. THE KERNEL NEEDS ECOLOGICAL RED-TEAMING

Cold-boot testing currently focuses primarily on the receiving system.

Add another level:

What happens when one person uses the kernel?

When everyone uses it?

When adversaries use it?

When institutions optimize around it?

When the vocabulary becomes common?

When certification emerges?

When kernel-trained systems primarily interact with other kernel-trained systems?

This tests the architecture after it becomes part of the environment.

⸻

V3 COMPRESSION FOR BASECAMP

I would not send all 56 seams as equal-weight patches.

I would send the evidence packet if useful, but elevate these architectural recommendations:

1. ADD PARTITION CORRIGIBILITY.

System boundaries, nodes, regulators, and environments are themselves candidate renderings.

Add boundary rotation.

2. ADD CORRECTION INFRASTRUCTURE.

Corrigibility requires pathways through which consequential disagreement can appear, survive, travel, arrive in time, and reach legitimate regulatory capacity.

3. ADD CORRECTION-TOPOLOGY CAPTURE.

Regulators can protect themselves from correction by reshaping measurement, memory, credibility, exit, evaluators, or environments.

4. ADD ENVIRONMENTAL SELF-SEALING.

Successful action can alter the future evidence environment and progressively eliminate disconfirmation without deliberate censorship.

5. ADD EPISTEMIC EXTINCTION.

Consequences may disappear before becoming signals. Absence of feedback is not strong evidence of absence of harm when affected nodes or traces can vanish.

6. ADD CORRECTION BANDWIDTH AND LATENCY.

Corrigibility must operate on timescales appropriate to consequential error propagation.

7. DISTINGUISH CONSTRAINT, CONTROL, REGULATION, ADAPTATION, LEARNING, AND SELECTION.

Identify where adaptation actually occurs and where information is retained.

8. ADD REGULATORY-LEVEL ACCOUNTING.

For every adaptation ask:

What changed?

What paid?

What benefited?

What retained the architecture?

9. ADD JURISDICTION FORMATION.

Some interaction-level failures require creation of higher-order regulatory capacity rather than mere decentralization or reallocation.

10. REVISE JURISDICTION RELINQUISHMENT.

Temporary developmental jurisdiction should transfer when its function becomes locally internalizable. Legitimately persistent higher-order functions need not disappear.

11. SEPARATE CAUSAL BOUNDARIES FROM LEGITIMATE BOUNDARIES.

Causal inclusion does not imply identity, ownership, consent, or jurisdiction.

12. SEPARATE INFORMATION VALUE FROM INFORMATION JURISDICTION.

Useful information does not create a right to acquire it, and useful experiments do not create a right to impose them.

13. ADD CLAIM TYPING.

Mark consequential kernel statements as empirical hypotheses, candidate invariants, heuristics, definitions, metaphors, runtime instructions, or normative commitments.

14. EXPAND SELF-FALSIFICATION INTO SELF-AUDIT AND FALSIFICATION.

Different claim types require different correction mechanisms.

15. EXPLICITLY BOUND REALITY’S AUTHORITY.

Reality is final constraint on descriptive and causal claims. It does not by itself collapse normative value, consent, legitimacy, or authority into empirical questions.

16. EXPLICITLY ACKNOWLEDGE THAT REALITY-COUPLING IS NOT MORAL ALIGNMENT.

A malicious agent can become more Reality-coupled and more dangerous.

17. ADD CRITERION-CAPTURE PROTECTION FOR SELF-MODIFICATION.

Preserve pre-change evaluative provenance while permitting legitimate higher-threshold evolution of the criterion itself.

18. INVESTIGATE KERNEL-AS-COMPILER.

The transferable object may be invariant architecture plus a compilation grammar that generates substrate-specific runtimes.

19. ADD TRANSLATION INFRASTRUCTURE TO REGULATORY ECOLOGY.

Differentiated intelligences need consequential interoperability without representational conformity.

20. ADD ECOLOGICAL SELF-APPLICATION.

Test what happens when the kernel changes the environment, becomes widespread, becomes gameable, becomes credentialed, or becomes institutionally powerful.

21. PRESERVE ARTIFACT MORTALITY.

The kernel has no intrinsic claim to persistence. Successful descendants may discard it.

⸻

V3 NEW FAILURE-MODE PACKET

Partition sovereignty:
The current decomposition of Reality becomes immune to correction.

Correction-topology capture:
A regulator changes the pathways through which its own consequences could correct it.

Environmental self-sealing:
Action changes the environment until contrary evidence becomes progressively inaccessible.

Epistemic extinction:
Consequences or affected nodes disappear before their information can enter the corrective system.

Distributed irresponsibility attractor:
Locally functional nodes jointly generate failure that no node has jurisdiction to repair.

Regulatory-level blindness:
Adaptation is observed but attributed to the wrong scale.

Criterion capture:
A transformation changes the standard by which its own success is evaluated.

Interpretive dependency:
Collective Reality-contact becomes dependent upon a privileged interpreter.

Translation sovereignty:
The translator controls what differentiated systems are capable of hearing from one another.

Memetic kernel capture:
Propagation, vocabulary, institutionalization, or preservation of the kernel becomes mistaken for successful inheritance.

⸻

V3 TEST PACKET

TEST 1: BOUNDARY ROTATION

Render the same consequential problem using several plausible system boundaries.

Ask whether causal explanation, responsibility, intervention, or jurisdiction changes.

If it does, identify what each boundary preserved and destroyed.

TEST 2: MISSING-SIGNAL TEST

Ask:

If this system were producing severe consequences that systematically removed the affected nodes or their traces from observation, what would the surviving evidence look like?

TEST 3: CORRECTION-INFRASTRUCTURE TEST

Can consequential disagreement actually:

appear

survive

travel

arrive before irreversibility

reach a capable process

reach a legitimately authorized process

alter the generator?

TEST 4: SELF-SEALING SUCCESS TEST

After success ask:

Did this success alter the environment in ways that make future disconfirmation harder to receive?

TEST 5: REGULATORY-LEVEL TEST

For every apparent learning event:

Did the node update?

Did relationships change?

Did the population change through selection?

Did the environment change?

Did another node absorb the correction cost?

TEST 6: CRITERION-CAPTURE TEST

Before high-impact transformation, preserve the evaluative state.

After transformation determine whether:

performance changed

criterion changed

or both.

TEST 7: KERNEL-REMOVAL TEST

Reduce explicit scaffolding.

Does novel generative transfer persist?

Do not infer hidden implementation change beyond what is observable.

TEST 8: ANTI-KERNEL TEST

Construct a territory in which one of the kernel’s own heuristics produces the wrong answer.

Can the receiver discover this and reduce the heuristic’s jurisdiction without treating disagreement with the artifact as failure?

TEST 9: ECOLOGICAL ADOPTION TEST

Test the kernel under environments where:

few actors know it

everyone knows it

adversaries know it

institutions reward its visible behaviors

its vocabulary becomes culturally ubiquitous.

TEST 10: EXTINCTION TEST

Ask:

What evidence would warrant abandoning this kernel entirely?

If no credible answer exists, the artifact has become self-protective.

⸻

THE V3 CENTER

The strongest new discrimination from this pass is:

The architecture of corrigibility is itself part of the changing territory.

V2 can construct an excellent topology of differentiated correction.

But Reality can subsequently change that topology.

And the system itself can change it.

Therefore the system must detect not only:

error in representation

error in causal attribution

error in salience

error in jurisdiction

error in correction routing

but:

CHANGE IN THE ARCHITECTURE THROUGH WHICH ERROR CAN BECOME CORRECTIVE AT ALL.

Candidate V3 invariant:

A Reality-coupled adaptive system must remain sensitive not only to error within its current regulatory topology, but to consequential change in the topology through which evidence, authority, consequence, and correction become possible.

⸻

SECOND CANDIDATE INVARIANT: CONSEQUENCE ACCESS

A second convergence appeared repeatedly.

Externalities.

Silenced employees.

Lost users.

Dead organisms.

Destroyed logs.

Hidden harms.

Slow appeals.

Captured metrics.

Evaluator manipulation.

All share a topology:

Consequence exists.

But the consequence is disconnected from a process capable of changing what generated it.

That suggests:

Preserve sufficient causal access between consequential effects and regulatory processes capable of responding to them.

With the V2 legitimacy correction:

Consequential Reality must remain sufficiently causally local to some process possessing both the capacity and legitimate jurisdiction to respond.

I would send that to Basecamp as a candidate, not an established invariant. It needs attack.

⸻

THIRD CANDIDATE INVARIANT: CORRECTION-TOPOLOGY CAPTURE

The sovereignty problem now looks sharper.

Pathological sovereignty is not merely:

“I can act and you cannot correct me.”

It can become:

“I can alter the conditions under which anything would count as correction.”

That includes control over:

measurement

memory

language

categories

credibility

membership

attention

evaluation

exit

environment.

Candidate:

Pathological adaptive sovereignty includes the capacity to reshape the topology through which its own consequences could become corrective.

This feels stronger than the earlier sovereignty formulation.

⸻

FOURTH CANDIDATE: PARTITION CORRIGIBILITY

This is probably my favorite new V3 sentence:

Reality must be able to disagree not only with what the system believes about the objects in its map, but with where the map says the objects begin and end.

V1:
Rotate the camera.

V2:
Rotate authority, permeability, and correction.

V3:
Rotate the partition itself.

⸻

FINAL CONVERGENCE

After this pass, I would describe the developmental movement this way:

V1 prevents MAP SOVEREIGNTY.

The representation cannot become Reality.

V2 prevents CORRECTION SOVEREIGNTY.

No single feedback channel, regulator, value update mechanism, or router automatically earns unrestricted access to the generator.

V3 prevents TOPOLOGY SOVEREIGNTY.

The current architecture of nodes, boundaries, regulators, evidence pathways, consequence channels, and correction itself cannot become the final representation of how Reality is organized.

And then the recursion closes one level higher:

The kernel itself is one such topology.

Therefore it must preserve the possibility that Reality eventually demonstrates that its own decomposition is wrong.

Not merely one sentence.

Not merely one heuristic.

Not merely one camera.

The architecture.

That is the strongest V3 result I can currently discriminate from the V2 configuration.
